question: Compare lung-enriched and skeletal-muscle-enriched proteins in the Human Protein Atlas. For each tissue-enriched cohort report its size, the share of FDA approved drug targets and the share secreted to blood, and test the overlap by reporting intersection size and Jaccard. Select the ten members of each cohort with the highest abundance in its own tissue, ties by Ensembl ID, and show their abundance in both tissues and main subcellular locations. Draw cohort-composition bars and a two-tissue abundance heatmap, with the supporting tables. For the union of the selected genes, also report all consensus interaction edges between them and each selected gene's degree within that union, treating edges as undirected, deduplicating and excluding self-edges; draw a degree bar chart. If a requested ranked list has fewer eligible members, return every eligible member and state the count. Use Ensembl genes present in the HPA master table as the gene universe and break all gene-ranking ties by Ensembl ID.

tool_uses.name: batch_protein_lookup
tool_uses.input: {"columns": ["Gene", "Ensembl", "Tissue RNA - lung [nTPM]", "Tissue RNA - skeletal muscle [nTPM]", "Subcellular location", "Protein class"], "genes": ["ACTA1", "ACTA2"], "format": "json"}

turns.text: I have the two high-expression tissue cohorts (lung n=68, skeletal muscle n=82, TSV verified as complete). Now I'll pull full tissue expression profiles for all 123 unique genes in batches of 10.
